title: MongoDB Documents and Repositories
summary: Map documents, use MongoRepository and handle IDs and indexes.

sources.title: Engineering Digest: Step-by-Step Tutorial: How to Integrate MongoDB in Your Spring Boot Application

richText: @Document selects a MongoDB collection. @Id maps a Java field to the document’s _id.
Use org.springframework.data.annotation.Id for MongoDB. jakarta.persistence.Id belongs to JPA and is a different annotation.
Spring Data maps fields to document values. Lombok can generate accessors, but Lombok does not configure persistence or validate an HTTP request.
A repository is the persistence interface used by your service. Spring Data creates its implementation as a Spring bean.
MongoRepository<JournalEntry, ObjectId> identifies the document type and its ID type. It supplies save, findById, findAll and deleteById.
Derived queries are queries built from method names. findByTitle searches the title property. A misspelled property can prevent repository creation.
Choose a derived method for a stable, simple query. Choose MongoTemplate when optional filters or explicit updates make a method name unclear.
Keep HTTP handling in the controller and business rules in a service. Inject the repository into that service.
save persists the document. A new document can receive a generated ID. Saving an existing ID can replace stored fields, so do not pass a partial request object directly as a replacement.
findById returns Optional because an ID may not exist. Convert absence into the API’s chosen response, such as 404.
Validate ObjectId text before constructing it at an HTTP boundary. A malformed ID differs from a valid ID with no matching document.
@Indexed(unique = true) describes a unique index. It enforces uniqueness only after the database index exists. Automatic index creation is disabled by default in Spring Data MongoDB.
Create required indexes deliberately. Existing duplicates can prevent a unique index from being created. A pre-save lookup alone cannot prevent concurrent duplicates.
